2.text: the town of Verkhoyansk. The Chukchee were quite eager to trade with the

3.text: Russians. They wanted Russian wares; above all, iron and tobacco: so the

4.text: Russians and the Chukchee agreed to meet every year in the spring-time for

5.text: trading-purposes, in some place to the east of the Kolyma. At first a place

6.text: on the Large Anui, at the mouth of its affluent the Angarka River, was

7.text: selected for this purpose. In the year 1805 Zashiversk was deprived of its

8.text: governing position, and the official centre of the Kolyma country removed to

9.text: Sredne-Kolymsk. A few years after that the Chukchee spring fair was also

11.text: Anui Fair. — A wooden fort was built and surrounded by palisades,

12.text: as was usual with the forts of former times. The Russians were still afraid

13.text: of the Chukchee, and wanted to be protected against sudden attacks; but the

14.text: attacks never occurred, and other fairs were arranged in the country of the

15.text: Gishiga, without any palisades, in a cluster of block-houses built for the purpose,

16.text: or even in the open tundra on the snow.

17.text: I obtained from the Chukchee a curious story about the beginning of

18.text: the Anui fair. According to that story, the Chukchee wanted trade so badly,

19.text: that they were ready to force the Russians to open it, even by personal

22.text: gathered, — Chukchee, Russians, Chuvantzy, — and wanted to begin bartering

26.text: accusation. ‘We did not do it. The people of Anadyr did it.’ Four strong

27.text: men walked around in the Russian fortress. There is nothing to do. They

28.text: peep into the house of the officer through a chink in the door quite attentively.

29.text: There he sits, clad in red, — red cap, red coat, red boots. One says,

30.text: ‘Let us break down this door and seize him!’ They broke the door, caught

31.text: the red man, and carried him to one of the camps. He cried out, calling

32.text: for rescue, but nobody heard his voice. The next morning the Russian people

33.text: made an outcry. The local officer requested that they give back the officer

34.text: of the Czarina. ‘No,’ said the Chukchee, ‘we must first open up trade.’
34.note: mz draft dropped both pairs of single curly quotes around 'No,' and 'we must first open up trade.'; supplied from the raster.

35.text: The four strong men released the captive, and, to appease his anger, they

36.text: gave him two black foxes. Then the people said, ‘We cannot trade without

37.text: an interpreter.’ So they found Keˊka, a man of Chuvantzy stock, who lived

38.text: on the Big River, and made him their interpreter.”²
